composition.rule: Expand every mandatory base and recovery row and every additional row. Merge only identical requirement IDs, using current operator wording for UX IDs; retain all distinct obligations. Every inherited row starts UNVERIFIED for this continuation regardless of older dispositions. Resolve source locations and production owners from their source register and reviewed bindings; a candidate mapping is not executed proof. Every row inherits the applicable stage/operation and evidence defaults below unless narrowed by its own controlling source. No mandatory row is removed.
composition.coverageDenominator: All distinct expanded mandatory rows, including this addendum. A row counts in the numerator only with a named executed case, expected result, actual result, command, untruncated raw output, and source revision.

defaults.applicableStages: Every stage to which the source requirement applies, derived from the actual workflow stage and dependency registries, including first and final stages.
defaults.requiredEvidence: Named executed positive and otherwise-valid single-violation cases derived from the controlling requirement; exact actual UI/file-transport observations where applicable; before/after source identities; raw untruncated output; affected downstream replay. Synthetic evidence must be labeled and does not establish real-project, independent-human, or physical-device acceptance.

independentOmissionReview.observed: The prior additional-prompt register explicitly enumerated UX-001 through UX-009 and the Stage 2 invariant, but not UX-010 through UX-020 or DEF-1 through DEF-9 as separate IDs. This addendum retains the prior rows and adds the current full operator obligations. The mechanically generated normative manifest itself labels candidate module/test mappings as unproven; those mappings are not promoted to PASS.
independentOmissionReview.remaining: Complete source-to-case reconciliation and exact final-revision execution remain required. This register makes no conformance or semantic-completeness claim.

rows.observableExpectedBehavior: The next correct action is visible without scrolling after any state change.
Completing a stage's operator work brings the next required reading or action into view.
Forward-progress auto-scroll moves downward; upward movement requires explicit return, correction, or retry and lands on the required action.
Saving project information confirms ingestion and directs the operator to the next required operation.
One operator action exports every required stage handoff file in a compatible transport after stage/version isolation is enforced.
Instruction text appears once per view without duplicates at every stage.
Original versus regenerated instruction state derives from actual attempt/revision state and never from an unconditional label.
A genuinely regenerated instruction is identified at the point of use.
Operator language is concise and imperative; redundant text, repeated controls, unnecessary confirmations and irrelevant current-task information are absent.
Required decisions, useful status, actionable errors and recovery remain visible; codes, internal identifiers, diagnostics and advanced tools are disclosed separately.
Confirmations are in-page and scrolled into view; no popup, modal, browser alert or browser confirmation is used.
History restoration restores the recorded view without automatic stage advancement.
Successful acceptance exposes the next required operation and concise Undo.
Every genuinely loading operation exceeding the single configurable threshold displays a visible compact indicator, including export, response import, restoration and pending operations.
A distinct minimal informative startup view is visible while startup loads; it is not the operation-loading element.
Every load resolves or visibly fails with an actionable error and recovery access; no indefinite indicator.
Loading is shown only for genuine loading, never for crashed, stalled or broken state.
In-flight controls are disabled and repeated activation cannot duplicate or enqueue work or corrupt recovery.
Completion, failure and recovery feedback is explicit for every operation.
Actual latency is measured and reported across the workflow; application-owned computation, assembly and coordination are automated.
Saving confirms ingested project data and exposes the next operation without repeated presses.
Every stage has no duplicate instruction text in or across simultaneously presented views.
First-generation instructions are not falsely described as regenerated.
Actual regeneration is identified to the operator.
Stage transport does not require three separate export actions.
Editing project input after accepted Stage 1 offers recoverable impact confirmation and commits or cancels consistently without crashing.
Slow exports, response imports and other operations show truthful loading feedback.
Startup is visibly distinguished from an empty or nonresponsive application.
Operation latency is measured and reported; reproduced unnecessary computational/assembly work is removed at its owner.
Permitted selection, inspection and execution, including completed stages, derive information and actions from the selected stage in the active version.
Executions and handoffs bind project, version, stage, operation, attempt and revision with relevant project inputs, rules and valid prerequisites.
Every agent-facing surface excludes all subsequent-stage information from both active work and retained history.
Copied content, derived summaries and shared files cannot indirectly disclose subsequent-stage information.
Changes to project version, stage, scope or governing revision rebuild stale handoffs.
Restoration backups remain separate from stage handoffs and isolation holds after selection, re-execution, Undo, Redo, browser traversal and History restoration.
Stage 2 directs inventory only to external published books, peer-reviewed journals, government reports and public websites, never internal repository files.
Selection, execution, response validation, committed acceptance and restoration remain distinct; selection/generation/receipt does not replace work or reset progress.
Validation precedes acceptance; a valid replacement stays a candidate until confirmation and successful commit.
In-page confirmation dynamically identifies actual replaced and transitively affected work and required redo from authoritative dependencies, not a fixed count or contiguous range.
Confirmation states that the previous version remains restorable; unaffected downstream work is not described as affected, and retained work is not described as permanently erased.
Cancellation or no answer preserves accepted work and progress; navigation, reload and restoration never auto-accept a candidate.
Commit rechecks exact candidate, active version, revision and consequences; changed state requires recomputation and reconfirmation.
A recoverable predecessor is saved before activation; acceptance/invalidation commit atomically across results, statuses, approvals, accounting, pending work, materials and delivery readiness.
Invalidate every required direct and indirect completed, partial and pending dependent while preserving established independent valid work.
Affected rework is performed and accepted against the replacement's upstream state; incompatible historical responses, approvals and artifacts cannot satisfy current requirements.
Repeated submission of a committed operation cannot accept again or repeat invalidation.
Opening a session checkpoints all pre-existing project state and meaningful later changes retain complete reconstructable versions.
Checkpoints retain inputs, responses, prerequisite relationships, acceptance records, progress, drafts and exact file contents; drafts/views are captured before leaving.
Durable application persistence, not browser history, URLs, file pickers or memory alone, provides recovery without unnecessary parallel persistence architecture.
Restore an internally compatible whole version, including matching downstream work or replacement invalidation; unaccepted candidates remain unaccepted.
Restoration activates saved state without rerunning commands or requiring repetition of retained completed work.
A new continuation after restoration preserves the previous continuation; compact History exposes retained alternatives without normal-workflow internal IDs or branch detail.
Undo, Redo, browser-history and History use compatible authoritative restoration; recovery outlives notifications and survives reload and required backup restore.

Atomic restoration handles rapid navigation, multi-entry jumps, interruption, missing/corrupt files and persistence failures; success is not reported before data availability and failure preserves recoverable state.
Authorization, concurrency, execution records and duplicate protection remain enforced; independent work in another tab/session is not silently overwritten.
Delayed abandoned operations cannot mutate restored versions; pending state reconciles actual status without repeating completed requests/deliveries or claiming external actions were undone.
Declared tested limits retain session-start recovery; History works without native entries; promised points are not silently discarded or advertised as unlimited.
A required checkpoint-save failure is reported before committing the dependent change.
Ordinary stage selection opens that stage in the active version and never implicitly rewinds because it is completed.
Each history entry binds saved version and view; traversal restores project, selected stage, position, decisions, working data, files and dependent progress, not merely labels.

Restoration uses the actual destination for any available history distance, repeated Back/Forward or direct retained-entry jump; traversal preserves remaining path and new continuations retain superseded versions in History.
Initial view, reload, direct links and supported mobile navigation work; saved-version links resolve that version under current access controls while ordinary stage links use active state.
Prerequisites are enforced within the active complete version and cannot be bypassed by combining incompatible approvals or data.
Entries outside the application retain normal browser behavior and navigation creates no trapping history loop.

rows.productionOwner: verification and relevant production owner for each defect
rows.observableExpectedBehavior: Each defect has recorded source revision, inputs, sequence, expected behavior and actual reproduction before repair.
Each defect has a retained regression that fails for the defect and passes in its absence on this candidate.

rows.productionOwner: authored production authority and every affected generator/consumer
rows.observableExpectedBehavior: Derived defects are corrected at their upstream authority and regenerated; the earliest responsible production layer and shared contract consumers are corrected, not patched symptoms.
Replay the failed operator path through actual controls and verify every affected downstream path.

Production, not tests alone, enforces ownership, stage boundaries, valid transitions, current version/scope, atomic mutation, retry identity and invalidation. Contract text versus register data, authored versus derived output, and fact versus decision remain distinct.
Expected outcomes are derived from the specification and operator requirements independently of implementation.
For every required gate class an otherwise valid disposable case with one deliberate violation is rejected for that violation; removing it permits progression.

Targeted ownership/context bypass, missing confirmation, incomplete invalidation, wrong byte comparison, retained-history mutation and incompatible restoration faults are caught by the relevant tests; restoration returns the suite green; uncaught faults create coverage-gap rows.

Applicable stage and transition coverage includes boundaries, repeat/movement, no downstream work, and completed/partial/pending/invalidated work; invalid, cancelled, unanswered, duplicate, stale, concurrent, failed-storage and interrupted-commit cases execute.

rows.productionOwner: verify-browser-recovery.mjs; context, history and file-byte suites
rows.observableExpectedBehavior: Generated and exported bytes prove inclusion/isolation after restoration; restored data, dependencies, approvals and files match checkpoints across reversals, alternatives, reloads, direct links, mobile gestures, backups, retention/corruption/interruption/concurrency and delayed operations.
Source matches, declared flags, screenshots alone and test-file presence are never substituted for behavioral correctness.

Generated sequences derive from real workflow rules and state combinations across progression, selection, history, re-execution, confirmation/cancel, restoration, alternatives, retry/duplicates/stale responses, corrections, reload, corruption/storage failure and concurrency, not a fixed demonstration path or distance.
After each operation check coherent active version, retained recovery, isolation, approvals and dependent-work status; demonstrate both rejection and successful valid completion.
Explore revision, confirmation, invalidation, restoration, transaction and authorization with declared bounds/assumptions; reduce and retain each discovered failure on this candidate.

Actual controls and file transport exercise exports, context transfer, ingestion, returned-file mapping, review/acceptance, app commands, persistence, correction, recovery, saved history and delivery, with prerequisites arising from prior operations.

rows.productionOwner: complete operator and recovery browser suites
rows.observableExpectedBehavior: Execute a complete valid project and all required correction/rejection/replacement/cancel/invalidation/recompletion/restoration/alternative/session-start/reload/interruption/backup-history/final-byte retrieval journeys at contract workloads and history lengths.

rows.productionOwner: stage, transition and requirement evidence registers
rows.observableExpectedBehavior: Journey coverage follows actual stages/dependencies/transitions and accounts for every applicable class rather than generalizing one example or jump distance.
Synthetic evidence is labeled; required real external outputs are separate; independence, human actions and device observations are asserted only when established.
Only this candidate exists; every discovered defect within dependency closure stays on it; no second branch, split closure, cherry-pick or broken-state deferral.
Merge only an unchanged integrated revision with complete required CI green, every claimed row PASS with executed evidence, no regression and no open defect in dependency closure.

rows.productionOwner: repository integration and Pages deployment controls
rows.observableExpectedBehavior: Merge one converged candidate, deploy and verify it before any next candidate; use normal integration/deployment controls.
Verify exact deployed source revision, resource identities, worker dependencies and running bytes.
Repeat deployment acceptance for isolation, confirmation, dependent recovery, reversible acceptance, History and browser navigation; later changes invalidate affected evidence.

Do not narrow requirements, conflate distinct obligations or hard-code stage ranges/distances/sequences; dependencies determine minimal complete correction while preserving working architecture and approved visuals.
Record and implement the broader reading where the specification does not resolve broad versus narrow readings; unresolved operator-reserved decisions remain explicit rather than silent.

Independently review omissions and retain every mandatory specification/operator/prohibition/failure/recovery/acceptance row with source, owner, expected behavior, evidence, scope and status; count only executed PASS rows over all mandatory rows; no unsupported removals.

rows.productionOwner: verification scripts, CI logs and reports
rows.observableExpectedBehavior: Every reported quantity derives from an executed command with raw untruncated output; PASS requires named executed actual versus predeclared expected result; no estimates, fabricated quantities or summaries substituted for output.

Precisely distinguish tested environments/limits, functional readiness, physical acceptance, production maturity, unavailable verification capability, operator decisions and reachable unmet application requirements.

rows.productionOwner: integration, deployment and final evidence report
rows.observableExpectedBehavior: Deliver the corrected verified deployed application, not an audit, plan, patch archive or isolated repair; terminal rows are executed PASS or genuinely operator-required, with all specified final evidence and remaining defects reported.
After real Save in each required viewport, both the actionable summary and its actual export button are visible without a test-driver scroll, including layout changes during operation completion.

Any proposed contract-text change requires operator approval; no contract-text modification is authorized or made by this addendum.
Establish approved visual baseline and evidence bound to final deployed revision; only demonstrated requirement-driven repairs are allowed.
Record any unresolved specification ambiguity and candidate readings for the operator rather than choosing silently.
Actual physical-iPhone Safari acceptance, device observations and visual comparison bound to exact final deployed revision; responsive Chromium is not this evidence.
Required real-project external-source outputs, genuine human actions and independently established observations; synthetic counterpart fixtures do not establish these.
